purpose: Prevents compromised, outdated, or untrustworthy components, dependencies, and build/deployment tooling from introducing vulnerabilities into the application.
summary: Software Supply Chain Failures occur when an application relies on third-party libraries, packages, base images, or CI/CD tooling that are outdated, vulnerable, or tampered with, allowing attackers to compromise the application indirectly through the software it's built and delivered with rather than a flaw in its own code.
expectedStatementElements: How dependencies (libraries, packages, base images) are inventoried and scanned for known vulnerabilities
How the organization decides when and how to patch or upgrade outdated or vulnerable components
What controls protect the CI/CD pipeline itself from tampering (build integrity, signed artifacts, restricted access)
How the provenance and integrity of third-party components are verified before they're incorporated
evidenceExamples: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) or dependency inventory with vulnerability scan results
Patch/upgrade cadence policy for outdated or vulnerable dependencies
CI/CD pipeline security controls (access restrictions, artifact signing, build integrity checks)
Documentation of the vetting process for new third-party dependencies before adoption
commonGaps: No current inventory or scanning exists for third-party dependencies and their known vulnerabilities
Known-vulnerable dependencies remain in use long after a fix is available, with no defined patch cadence
CI/CD pipeline access and build integrity aren't protected, allowing tampering to go undetected
New dependencies are adopted without any vetting of their source, maintenance status, or trustworthiness
interviewQuestions: Do you have a current inventory of every dependency this application uses, and are they scanned for known vulnerabilities?
When a dependency has a known vulnerability, how quickly does it actually get patched?
What stops someone from tampering with your build pipeline and slipping in a malicious change?
What's your process for vetting a new third-party library before it's added to the project?
